questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is Panchayati Raj?

options.A: A system of urban local self-government
options.B: A system of rural local self-government through elected institutions at village, intermediate and district levels
options.C: A system of state government administration
options.D: A system of central government administration

questions.explanation: Panchayati Raj is a system of rural local self-government through elected institutions at village, intermediate and district levels, intended to enable people to participate in local administration and development.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does the term Panchayati Raj mean?

options.A: A system of village-based democratic local governance through Panchayats

questions.explanation: The term Panchayati Raj refers to a system of village-based democratic local governance through Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is rural local self-government?

options.A: Administration of local rural affairs by elected local bodies exercising powers assigned by the Constitution and State laws
options.B: Administration of rural areas by central government officials
options.C: Administration of rural areas by state government officials
options.D: Administration of rural areas by private bodies

questions.explanation: Rural local self-government is the administration of local rural affairs by elected local bodies that exercise powers and responsibilities assigned by the Constitution and State laws.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the main objective of Panchayati Raj?

options.B: Democratic decentralisation by transferring functions, funds and functionaries to elected rural local bodies
options.C: Increasing state government control over villages
options.D: Reducing people's participation in local administration

questions.explanation: The main objective of Panchayati Raj is democratic decentralisation: transferring appropriate functions, funds and functionaries to elected rural local bodies so that people can participate in decisions affecting their villages.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Directive Principle refers to the organisation of village Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 40 of the Constitution directs the State to organise village Panchayats and endow them with powers and authority necessary to function as units of self-government.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which committee recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system in India?
questions.explanation: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, appointed in 1957, recommended a three-tier system of democratic decentralisation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What was the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's central recommendation?

options.A: Two-tier system with Mandal Panchayat and Zilla Parishad
options.B: Three-tier structure consisting of village, block and district-level institutions with Panchayat Samiti at block level as key executive body
options.C: Constitutional recognition for Panchayati Raj Institutions

questions.explanation: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended democratic decentralisation through a three-tier structure consisting of village, block and district-level institutions, with the Panchayat Samiti at the block level as the key executive body.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Where was the first formal Panchayati Raj system inaugurated in India?
questions.explanation: The first formal Panchayati Raj system was inaugurated at Nagaur in Rajasthan on 2 October 1959.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who inaugurated the Panchayati Raj system at Nagaur in 1959?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated the Panchayati Raj system at Nagaur in 1959.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which committee recommended constitutional recognition for Panchayati Raj Institutions in 1986?
questions.explanation: The L. M. Singhvi Committee, appointed in 1986, recommended constitutional recognition and protection for Panchayati Raj Institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which committee recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj structure in 1978?
questions.explanation: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a two-tier structure consisting of the Mandal Panchayat and Zilla Parishad.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the difference between Panchayati Raj and rural development administration?

options.A: Panchayati Raj refers to elected rural local self-government institutions, whereas rural development administration includes wider government departments, officials and schemes
options.C: Panchayati Raj is a central government scheme
options.D: Rural development administration refers to elected bodies only

questions.explanation: Panchayati Raj refers to elected rural local self-government institutions, whereas rural development administration includes the wider government departments, officials and schemes working in rural areas.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act?

options.A: An amendment giving constitutional status to Municipalities
options.B: An amendment giving constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions and inserting Part IX and Eleventh Schedule
options.C: An amendment related to fundamental rights
options.D: An amendment related to election commission

questions.explanation: The Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions and inserted Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule into the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: When was the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act passed by Parliament?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act was passed by Parliament in December 1992.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: When did the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act receive the President's assent?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act received the President's assent on 20 April 1993.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: When did the 73rd Constitutional Amendment come into force?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Why is 24 April observed as National Panchayati Raj Day in India?

options.A: Because the 73rd Constitutional Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993
options.B: Because the 73rd Constitutional Amendment was passed on 24 April 1993
options.C: Because the first Panchayati Raj system was inaugurated on 24 April 1959
options.D: Because the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed on 24 April 1957

questions.explanation: 24 April is observed as National Panchayati Raj Day because the 73rd Constitutional Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which part of the Constitution was inserted by the 73rd Amendment?
questions.explanation: Part IX, titled 'The Panchayats', was inserted into the Constitution by the 73rd Amendment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles are covered by Part IX of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part IX covers Articles 243 to 243-O.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Schedule was added by the 73rd Amendment?
questions.explanation: The Eleventh Schedule was added to the Constitution by the 73rd Amendment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule?
questions.explanation: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects that may be devolved to Panchayats by State legislatures.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article provides for Gram Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 243A provides for the Gram Sabha and authorises the State Legislature to prescribe its powers and functions by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article provides for the constitution of Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243B provides for the constitution of Panchayats at village, intermediate and district levels, subject to the constitutional exception for States with a population not exceeding 20 lakh regarding the intermediate tier.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article deals with the composition of Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243C deals with the composition of Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article provides for reservation of seats in Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243D provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women in Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article provides for the duration of Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243E provides that every Panchayat shall continue for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting unless sooner dissolved under law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article deals with disqualifications for membership of Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243F deals with disqualifications for membership of Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article deals with powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243G authorises State Legislatures to endow Panchayats with powers and responsibilities to function as institutions of self-government.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article deals with taxation powers and funds of Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243H deals with the power of Panchayats to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees, and with Panchayat funds and grants-in-aid, as provided by State law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article provides for the State Finance Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 243I provides for the constitution of a State Finance Commission to review the financial position of Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article deals with audit of Panchayat accounts?
questions.explanation: Article 243J deals with the maintenance and audit of Panchayat accounts.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article provides for the State Election Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 243K provides for the superintendence, direction and control of Panchayat elections by the State Election Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article deals with application of Part IX to Union Territories?
questions.explanation: Article 243L deals with the application of Part IX to Union Territories.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article deals with exceptions and excluded areas?
questions.explanation: Article 243M provides for areas and States to which Part IX does not apply, subject to the provisions stated in that article.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article deals with the continuance of existing laws and Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243N deals with the continuance of existing laws and Panchayats for the specified transitional period.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional article bars court interference in Panchayat electoral matters?
questions.explanation: Article 243O bars court interference in specified electoral matters, including challenges to delimitation laws, and provides that Panchayat elections may be questioned only through an election petition in the manner prescribed by State law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the significance of the 73rd Amendment?

options.A: It made Panchayats a constitutionally recognised level of democratic governance, prescribed regular elections and reservations, created the framework for State Finance Commissions and State Election Commissions, and listed 29 subjects for possible devolution
options.C: It gave constitutional status to Municipalities
options.D: It transferred all powers to the central government

questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment made Panchayats a constitutionally recognised level of democratic governance, prescribed regular elections and reservations, created the framework for State Finance Commissions and State Election Commissions, and listed 29 subjects for possible devolution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article defines Gram Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 243(b) defines Gram Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is a Gram Sabha?

options.A: A body consisting of all persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of a village-level Panchayat
options.B: A body of elected representatives only
options.D: A body of village elders only

questions.explanation: A Gram Sabha is the body consisting of all persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of a village-level Panchayat.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the powers of Gram Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 243A provides that a Gram Sabha may exercise such powers and perform such functions at village level as the State Legislature provides by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who are the members of a Gram Sabha?

options.A: All persons whose names are included in the electoral rolls for the relevant village area
options.B: Only elected members of the Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: All persons whose names are included in the electoral rolls for the relevant village area are members of the Gram Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Is Gram Sabha an elected body?

options.A: Yes, it is an elected body
options.B: No, it is a general body of registered electors of the village
options.C: Yes, it is elected by the Gram Panchayat
options.D: Yes, it is elected by the State Government

questions.explanation: No. Gram Sabha is a general body of registered electors of the village; it is not a body made up only of elected representatives.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the difference between Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat?

options.A: Gram Sabha consists of all registered voters in the village area, while Gram Panchayat is the elected local-government body for that area
options.C: Gram Panchayat consists of all registered voters, while Gram Sabha is the elected body
options.D: Gram Sabha is a state government body, while Gram Panchayat is a central government body

questions.explanation: Gram Sabha consists of all registered voters in the village area, while Gram Panchayat is the elected local-government body for that area.

questions.question: What is the importance of Gram Sabha in village democracy?

options.D: It has no role in village democracy

questions.explanation: Gram Sabha provides a direct forum for villagers to discuss local needs, scrutinise development activities, participate in planning and hold the Gram Panchayat accountable.

questions.question: What are the common functions of Gram Sabha under State laws?

questions.question: Does the Constitution itself prescribe a uniform number of Gram Sabha meetings each year?

options.B: Yes, the Constitution prescribes six meetings per year

questions.question: What is a Habitation Sabha in Karnataka?

questions.question: What is the difference between Gram Sabha and Ward Sabha?

questions.question: What is a Gram Panchayat?

options.B: A body of all registered voters in the village

questions.question: Which Article provides for village-level Panchayats?

questions.question: How is a Gram Panchayat area determined?

options.B: It has no role in maintaining village assets

questions.question: What is the role of Gram Panchayat in sanitation?

options.B: It has no role in drinking water

questions.question: What is the role of Gram Panchayat in beneficiary selection?

questions.question: What is the Panchayat Development Officer (PDO) in Karnataka?

questions.question: Who is the Upadhyaksha of a Gram Panchayat?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are obligatory or essential civic functions of local Panchayats commonly concerned with?

options.A: Local sanitation, drainage, drinking-water facilities, village roads, public lighting, maintenance of community assets and public health-related activities, as specified by State law

questions.explanation: Obligatory or essential civic functions commonly include local sanitation, drainage, drinking-water facilities, village roads, public lighting, maintenance of community assets and public health-related activities, as specified by State law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are developmental functions of Panchayats?

options.A: Local agricultural development, irrigation and watershed works, poverty alleviation, rural housing facilitation, education support, livelihood promotion and implementation of development schemes

questions.explanation: Developmental functions include local agricultural development, irrigation and watershed works, poverty alleviation, rural housing facilitation, education support, livelihood promotion and implementation of development schemes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are regulatory functions of Gram Panchayats?

options.A: Depending on State law, they may include regulation of local buildings, public places, markets, trades, sanitation and protection of public property

questions.explanation: Depending on State law, regulatory functions of Gram Panchayats may include regulation of local buildings, public places, markets, trades, sanitation and protection of public property.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the difference between a function and a power of a Panchayat?

options.A: A function is a duty or area of responsibility assigned to the Panchayat, while a power is the legal authority needed to perform that function
options.C: A function is a legal authority, while a power is a duty
options.D: A function is a tax, while a power is a fee

questions.explanation: A function is a duty or area of responsibility assigned to the Panchayat, while a power is the legal authority needed to perform that function, such as making decisions, collecting a tax or regulating an activity.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are functionaries in the context of Panchayati Raj?

options.A: The officers, employees and technical staff required to carry out the responsibilities assigned to Panchayats

questions.explanation: Functionaries are the officers, employees and technical staff required to carry out the responsibilities assigned to Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does the principle of subsidiarity mean in local governance?

options.A: A public function should be performed by the lowest level of government that can carry it out effectively, with higher levels supporting tasks that require wider coordination or capacity
options.B: All functions should be performed by the central government
options.C: All functions should be performed by the state government
options.D: All functions should be performed by the highest level of government

questions.explanation: The principle of subsidiarity means that a public function should be performed by the lowest level of government that can carry it out effectively, with higher levels supporting tasks that require wider coordination or capacity.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article deals with the financial powers and funds of Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243H deals with the power to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees and with grants and Panchayat funds, as provided by State law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are the main sources of Panchayat revenue?

options.A: Own-source revenue such as taxes, rates, fees and user charges; assigned or shared State revenues; grants-in-aid; scheme funds; and other lawful receipts

questions.explanation: Main sources include own-source revenue such as taxes, rates, fees and user charges; assigned or shared State revenues; grants-in-aid; scheme funds; and other lawful receipts.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is own-source revenue of a Panchayat?

options.A: Income raised directly by the Panchayat through taxes, fees, rates, rents and user charges authorised by law
options.B: Grants received from the State Government
options.C: Grants received from the Union Government

questions.explanation: Own-source revenue is income raised directly by the Panchayat through taxes, fees, rates, rents and user charges authorised by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are assigned revenues?

options.A: Taxes, duties, tolls or fees collected by the State Government but allocated wholly or partly to Panchayats under State law
options.B: Taxes collected by the Panchayat directly
options.C: Grants received from the Union Government

questions.explanation: Assigned revenues are taxes, duties, tolls or fees collected by the State Government but allocated wholly or partly to Panchayats under State law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are grants-in-aid to Panchayats?

options.A: Financial transfers provided by the Union or State Government to support Panchayat functions and services, subject to conditions where applicable
options.B: Taxes collected by the Panchayat directly

questions.explanation: Grants-in-aid are financial transfers provided by the Union or State Government to support Panchayat functions and services, subject to conditions where applicable.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the State Finance Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 243I provides for the constitution of a State Finance Commission to review the financial position of Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who constitutes the State Finance Commission?

options.C: The Chief Minister of the State
options.D: The Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The Governor of the State constitutes the State Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How frequently must a State Finance Commission be constituted?
questions.explanation: A State Finance Commission must be constituted every five years.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Does the Union Finance Commission also make recommendations concerning Panchayat resources?

options.A: Yes, under Article 280(3)(bb), the Union Finance Commission recommends measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats
options.B: No, the Union Finance Commission has no role in Panchayat resources

questions.explanation: Yes. Under Article 280(3)(bb), the Union Finance Commission recommends measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats, based on recommendations of the State Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article deals with audit of Panchayat accounts?
questions.explanation: Article 243J provides for maintenance and audit of Panchayat accounts as prescribed by State law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Why is budgeting important for Panchayats?

options.A: A budget estimates expected receipts and expenditure, sets spending priorities, supports financial discipline and enables public accountability
options.B: A budget is only a legal formality
options.C: A budget is prepared only by the State Government
options.D: A budget is not required for Panchayats

questions.explanation: A budget estimates expected receipts and expenditure, sets spending priorities, supports financial discipline and enables public accountability.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is a tied grant?

options.A: A grant that must be spent on specified purposes or sectors prescribed by the funding authority
options.B: A grant that can be spent on any purpose
options.C: A grant given only to Zilla Panchayats
options.D: A grant given only to Gram Panchayats

questions.explanation: A tied grant is a grant that must be spent on specified purposes or sectors prescribed by the funding authority.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is an untied grant?

options.A: A grant that provides greater flexibility to the local body to spend funds on locally identified priorities within the permitted legal framework
options.B: A grant that must be spent on specified purposes
options.C: A grant given only to Zilla Panchayats
options.D: A grant given only to Gram Panchayats

questions.explanation: An untied grant provides greater flexibility to the local body to spend funds on locally identified priorities within the permitted legal framework.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the difference between the State Finance Commission and the Union Finance Commission?

options.A: The State Finance Commission reviews and recommends the distribution of State resources to local bodies, while the Union Finance Commission recommends Union-level fiscal transfers, including measures to augment State funds for Panchayats and Municipalities
options.C: The Union Finance Commission reviews State resources, while the State Finance Commission recommends Union-level transfers
options.D: The State Finance Commission conducts elections, while the Union Finance Commission prepares the budget

questions.explanation: The State Finance Commission reviews and recommends the distribution of State resources to local bodies, while the Union Finance Commission recommends Union-level fiscal transfers, including measures to augment State funds for Panchayats and Municipalities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the importance of financial devolution?

options.A: Financial devolution gives Panchayats the resources needed to carry out devolved functions and reduces excessive dependence on higher levels of government
options.B: Financial devolution increases dependence on higher levels of government
options.C: Financial devolution reduces the functions of Panchayats

questions.explanation: Financial devolution gives Panchayats the resources needed to carry out devolved functions and reduces excessive dependence on higher levels of government.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for Panchayat elections?
questions.explanation: Article 243K provides for the State Election Commission to supervise, direct and control Panchayat elections.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner?

options.C: The Chief Minister of the State
options.D: The Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The Governor appoints the State Election Commissioner, subject to the constitutional provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who supervises and controls Panchayat elections?
questions.explanation: The State Election Commission supervises, directs and controls the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of Panchayat elections.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Are Panchayat elections conducted by the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Yes, the Election Commission of India conducts Panchayat elections
options.B: No, Panchayat elections are conducted by the respective State Election Commission
options.C: Yes, the Election Commission of India conducts Panchayat elections in some states
options.D: No, Panchayat elections are conducted by the Union Government

questions.explanation: No. Panchayat elections are conducted by the respective State Election Commission, not the Election Commission of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the normal duration of a Panchayat?

options.C: Five years from the date appointed for its first meeting

questions.explanation: The normal duration is five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, under Article 243E.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: When should elections be completed if a Panchayat completes its five-year term?

options.A: Elections must be completed before the expiry of the five-year duration
options.B: Elections can be held after six months of expiry
options.C: Elections can be held after one year of expiry

questions.explanation: Elections must be completed before the expiry of the five-year duration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the deadline for holding elections after premature dissolution of a Panchayat?

options.A: Within three months from the date of dissolution
options.B: Within six months from the date of dissolution, unless the remainder of the original term is less than six months
options.C: Within one year from the date of dissolution
options.D: Within two years from the date of dissolution

questions.explanation: Elections must generally be held within six months from the date of dissolution, unless the remainder of the original term is less than six months; a Panchayat elected after dissolution serves only for the remainder of that period.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can a Panchayat be dissolved before completing five years?

options.A: No, a Panchayat cannot be dissolved before five years
options.B: Yes, it may be dissolved in accordance with State law, but constitutional safeguards require elections within the prescribed period
options.C: Yes, it may be dissolved only by the President
options.D: Yes, it may be dissolved only by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Yes. A Panchayat may be dissolved in accordance with State law, but constitutional safeguards require elections within the prescribed period.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the minimum age for contesting a Panchayat election under Article 243F?
questions.explanation: A person must have attained 21 years of age; a person is not disqualified merely because they are below 25 years.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is an electoral roll?

options.A: The official list of eligible voters for the relevant electoral area
options.B: The list of candidates contesting elections

questions.explanation: An electoral roll is the official list of eligible voters for the relevant electoral area.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is delimitation of Panchayat constituencies?

options.A: The process of determining territorial constituencies and allocating seats according to population and applicable legal rules
options.D: The process of appointing election officials

questions.explanation: Delimitation is the process of determining territorial constituencies and allocating seats according to population and applicable legal rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can a Panchayat election be challenged through an ordinary court case before the election is completed?

options.A: Yes, an ordinary court case can be filed
options.B: No, Article 243O restricts court interference in specified electoral matters; an election can be challenged only through an election petition in the manner prescribed by State law
options.C: Yes, a writ petition can be filed in the High Court
options.D: Yes, a PIL can be filed in the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: No. Article 243O restricts court interference in specified electoral matters; an election can be challenged only through an election petition in the manner prescribed by State law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is an election petition?

options.A: The legal procedure prescribed by State law to challenge the validity of a Panchayat election on specified grounds

questions.explanation: An election petition is the legal procedure prescribed by State law to challenge the validity of a Panchayat election on specified grounds.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is a by-election in Panchayati Raj?

options.A: An election held to fill a casual vacancy in a Panchayat seat before the end of the normal term, according to the applicable election law
options.B: An election held after the normal term
options.C: An election held along with general elections
options.D: An election held only for the Zilla Panchayat

questions.explanation: A by-election is held to fill a casual vacancy in a Panchayat seat before the end of the normal term, according to the applicable election law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for reservation in Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 243D provides for reservation of seats in Panchayats.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Are seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Panchayats?

options.A: No, there is no reservation for SCs and STs
options.B: Yes, seats are reserved for SCs and STs in proportion, as nearly as practicable, to their population in the Panchayat area
options.C: Yes, seats are reserved for SCs and STs in equal proportion
options.D: Yes, seats are reserved for SCs and STs at the discretion of the State Government

questions.explanation: Yes. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion, as nearly as practicable, to their population in the Panchayat area.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the minimum constitutional reservation for women in Panchayats?

options.A: One-fourth of the total number of seats
options.B: One-third of the total number of seats
options.C: One-half of the total number of seats
options.D: Two-thirds of the total number of seats

questions.explanation: Not less than one-third of the total number of seats to be filled by direct election must be reserved for women, including the seats reserved for women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Does the constitutional reservation for women also apply to offices of chairpersons?

options.A: No, it applies only to seats
options.B: Yes, not less than one-third of the total number of offices of chairpersons at each level of Panchayat must be reserved for women, in the manner prescribed by State law
options.C: Yes, but only at the Gram Panchayat level
options.D: Yes, but only at the Zilla Panchayat level

questions.explanation: Yes. Not less than one-third of the total number of offices of chairpersons at each level of Panchayat must be reserved for women, in the manner prescribed by State law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Can States provide more than one-third reservation for women in Panchayats?

options.A: No, States cannot provide more than one-third reservation
options.B: Yes, State legislatures may provide a higher percentage of reservation for women, subject to constitutional and legal requirements
options.C: Yes, but only with the approval of the President
options.D: Yes, but only with the approval of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Yes. State legislatures may provide a higher percentage of reservation for women, subject to constitutional and legal requirements.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the reservation for women in Karnataka Panchayati Raj Institutions?
questions.explanation: Karnataka provides 50 per cent reservation for women in seats and offices across all three tiers under amendments to the Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Karnataka amendment introduced 50 per cent reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions?
questions.explanation: The Karnataka Panchayat Raj Act was amended through the Karnataka Act 34 of 2011, giving effect to 50 per cent reservation for women.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Are chairperson offices also reserved for women in Karnataka?

options.A: No, chairperson offices are not reserved for women
options.B: Yes, the Karnataka Act provides for not less than 50 per cent of the offices of Adhyaksha and Upadhyaksha to be reserved for women, subject to the statutory provisions and rotation
options.C: Yes, but only one-third of chairperson offices are reserved for women
options.D: Yes, but only at the Gram Panchayat level

questions.explanation: Yes. The Karnataka Act provides for not less than 50 per cent of the offices of Adhyaksha and Upadhyaksha to be reserved for women, subject to the statutory provisions and rotation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Are seats reserved for Backward Classes under the Constitution itself?

options.A: Yes, the Constitution mandates reservation for Backward Classes
options.B: No, Article 243D(6) permits State Legislatures to make provisions for reservation of seats or offices of chairpersons in favour of Backward Classes; the detailed reservation depends on State law and applicable judicial and legal limits
options.C: Yes, but only at the Gram Panchayat level
options.D: Yes, but only at the Zilla Panchayat level

questions.explanation: Article 243D(6) permits State Legislatures to make provisions for reservation of seats or offices of chairpersons in favour of Backward Classes; the detailed reservation depends on State law and applicable judicial and legal limits.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How are reserved seats for SCs and STs determined?

options.A: They are allocated in proportion, as nearly as practicable, to the population of SCs and STs in the relevant Panchayat area
options.B: They are allocated equally among all Panchayats
options.C: They are allocated at the discretion of the State Government
options.D: They are allocated at the discretion of the Zilla Panchayat

questions.explanation: Reserved seats for SCs and STs are allocated in proportion, as nearly as practicable, to the population of SCs and STs in the relevant Panchayat area.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is rotation of reserved constituencies?

options.A: Changing the constituencies or offices assigned to particular reservation categories between elections according to prescribed rules, so that reservation opportunities are distributed across areas over time

questions.explanation: Rotation means changing the constituencies or offices assigned to particular reservation categories between elections according to prescribed rules, so that reservation opportunities are distributed across areas over time.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Why is reservation important in Panchayati Raj?

options.A: Reservation improves representation and participation of historically disadvantaged communities and women in local decision-making
options.B: Reservation reduces participation of disadvantaged communities
options.C: Reservation is only a legal formality

questions.explanation: Reservation improves representation and participation of historically disadvantaged communities and women in local decision-making.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the constitutional minimum reservation for women in Panchayats?
questions.explanation: The Constitution mandates a minimum one-third reservation for women in Panchayats. Karnataka provides 50 per cent under its State law. Do not confuse the constitutional minimum with the higher Karnataka provision.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the Karnataka provision for reservation for women in Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Karnataka provides 50 per cent reservation for women under its State law, which is higher than the constitutional minimum of one-third.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is decentralisation?

options.A: The transfer of decision-making authority, responsibilities and resources from higher levels of government to lower levels or local institutions
options.B: The concentration of power at the central level
options.C: The transfer of power from lower to higher levels

questions.explanation: Decentralisation is the transfer of decision-making authority, responsibilities and resources from higher levels of government to lower levels or local institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is democratic decentralisation?

options.A: Transfer of authority to elected local bodies and strengthening participation, representation and accountability at the local level
options.B: Transfer of authority to appointed officials
options.C: Concentration of power at the central level

questions.explanation: Democratic decentralisation transfers authority to elected local bodies and strengthens participation, representation and accountability at the local level.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the difference between deconcentration and devolution?

options.A: Deconcentration redistributes administrative tasks within the same government hierarchy, whereas devolution transfers meaningful authority and responsibility to elected autonomous local institutions
options.C: Deconcentration transfers authority to elected local bodies, whereas devolution redistributes administrative tasks
options.D: Deconcentration is a constitutional principle, whereas devolution is a statutory principle

questions.explanation: Deconcentration redistributes administrative tasks within the same government hierarchy, whereas devolution transfers meaningful authority and responsibility to elected autonomous local institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are the three Fs of Panchayati Raj decentralisation?

options.C: Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties and Directive Principles

questions.explanation: The three Fs of Panchayati Raj decentralisation are Functions, Funds and Functionaries.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does devolution of functions mean?

options.A: Assigning specific responsibilities and decision-making powers to Panchayats for local governance and development

questions.explanation: Devolution of functions means assigning specific responsibilities and decision-making powers to Panchayats for local governance and development.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does devolution of funds mean?

options.A: Providing Panchayats with adequate financial resources to perform their assigned functions

questions.explanation: Devolution of funds means providing Panchayats with adequate financial resources to perform their assigned functions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does devolution of functionaries mean?

options.A: Making the required government staff and technical personnel available to Panchayats for carrying out their responsibilities

questions.explanation: Devolution of functionaries means making the required government staff and technical personnel available to Panchayats for carrying out their responsibilities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Why are the three Fs important?

options.A: Panchayats cannot perform devolved responsibilities effectively unless they receive corresponding functions, financial resources and staff support
options.D: They are important only for the Zilla Panchayat

questions.explanation: Panchayats cannot perform devolved responsibilities effectively unless they receive corresponding functions, financial resources and staff support.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is participatory planning?

options.A: A process in which residents and local institutions identify needs, set priorities and contribute to development plans
options.B: A process in which only government officials prepare plans
options.C: A process in which only elected representatives prepare plans
options.D: A process in which only the central government prepares plans

questions.explanation: Participatory planning is a process in which residents and local institutions identify needs, set priorities and contribute to development plans.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is GPDP?

options.A: A participatory annual development plan prepared by a Gram Panchayat by assessing local needs, available resources and priorities, with community participation

questions.explanation: GPDP is a participatory annual development plan prepared by a Gram Panchayat by assessing local needs, available resources and priorities, with community participation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the role of Gram Sabha in GPDP?

options.A: The Gram Sabha provides a forum for discussing needs, prioritising works, reviewing proposals and strengthening public ownership of the village development plan
options.B: The Gram Sabha prepares the GPDP alone
options.C: The Gram Sabha has no role in GPDP
options.D: The Gram Sabha only approves the GPDP

questions.explanation: The Gram Sabha provides a forum for discussing needs, prioritising works, reviewing proposals and strengthening public ownership of the village development plan.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution

questions.question: What is the title of the deputy chairperson of a Karnataka Grama Panchayat?
questions.explanation: The deputy chairperson of a Karnataka Grama Panchayat is called the Upadhyaksha.
